Normal Attack
Performs up to 4 attacks using Wind Spirits, dealing Anemo DMG.

_curatorNotes: C1 (Clustered Vacuum Field) grants +1 skill charge → 2 total at C1+ (gcsim sucrose.go: Cons>=1 → SetNumCharges(ActionSkill, 2)). Authored as a chargeModifiers flat +1. E key = 56 = skillFrames[ActionSkill] (E→E cancel), added to frames alongside.

[Hexerei] Small Wind Spirit party DMG bonus is count-gated (gcsim internal/characters/sucrose/asc.go:113-141 hexOnSkill — IsHexerei && GetHexereiCount() >= 2), 0.0571428 DmgP to every Chars() entry for 15*60 frames. Authored in factionBonuses as allDmgBonus 5.71428 / 15s / target team. gcsim restricts the mod to AttackTagNormal/Extra/Plunge/ElementalArt/ElementalArtHold/ElementalBurst — swirl and other reaction DMG are excluded; allDmgBonus over-covers, hence the caveat.

↻ CAVEAT REMOVED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass, Nate-approved): no pixel — The Secret Rite team buff bar drawn from her E (factionBonuses onCast skill, allDmgBonus 5.71%, 15s, team) prints an ALL-DMG claim; gcsim restricts it to Normal/Charged/Plunge/Skill/Burst attack tags, so the bar over-claims by covering swirl and other reaction DMG. Same blessed shape as the 'shown as All Elemental RES' example. Category: visible-divergence.

abilities.name: Forbidden Creation - Isomer 75 / Type II

_curatorNotes: gcsim burst.go Burst(): AttackInfo 'Forbidden Creation-Isomer 75/Type II' — Element Anemo, Durability 25, Mult burstDot[c.TalentLvlBurst()]; burstDot[9] = 2.664 in zz_sucrose.dm.go (// burst: ForbiddenCreationIsomer75TypeII - DoT). Sidecar docs/curation/talents/sucrose.json burst row 'DoT' 10th value = 266.4% — agrees.

Cadence from the loop `for i := 137; i <= duration+5; i += 113` (duration = 360 at C0): 113f = 1.883s interval, first tick at cast-frame 137. Authored summon spawnsAt is also 137, so firstTickDelay = (137 - 137) / 60 = 0.
ICD: ICDTag ICDTagNone in burst.go, and frames-diff §5 measured 3/3 `none` — hence icdGate 'none' (every tick applies).
stat: atk — snapshot is c.Snapshot(&ai) with no stat substitution.

Tick COUNT: gcsim emits 3 ticks at C0 (137/250/363) and 4 at C2 (duration 480 → +476f). ↻ 2026-08-18 — THIS IS NO LONGER A LIVE RESIDUAL. The geometry is still as authored (our `duration` counts from SPAWN, gcsim's status counts from CAST, so the 6s window 137→497f would derive one tick too many at each tier — 4 at C0, 5 at C2) but the derived count is no longer what fires: the `tickCap: 3` / `tickCapScaling.ticks: 4` below, added by the tick-cap round the same day, clamps it to exactly gcsim's 3 and 4. ⛔ Do NOT read this note as an outstanding over-count and ⛔ do not 'fix' it by nudging the authored 6s duration — a cap is a COUNT, deliberately not a time bound, and the duration is the kit-stated lifetime.
The Elemental Absorption ticks (burstAbsorb, aiAbs, same 113f cadence, absorbed element) remain unmodelled — see the ability-level curator note.

tickCap 3 / 4 at C2 (tick-cap round, 2026-08-18): gcsim burst.go `for i := 137; i <= duration+5; i += 113` with `duration := 360` (480 at C2) gives three ticks base and four at C2. Our duration-derived 4 was one long at C0 and correct at C2, so the C2 override exists to keep the constellation case from being clamped by the base cap.

⚠️ The cap reaches the PLANNER and the GAUGE only. `tickCapOf` (src/lib/sim/summons.ts:203) is read by `collectSummonTicks` and by aura.ts's tick chain — the summon-lane markers, the PNG and the applications. It is NOT published to the Team Builder: `DerivedCapability.summon` carries `tickInterval`/`firstTickDelay` and no count (src/lib/capabilities/deriveCapabilities.ts `summonHost`), and Compare re-derives its own marks from interval-until-uptime (team-builder/lib/compare.ts `tickOffsets`, :201-205). So Compare still draws FOUR marks for this summon at C0 where the timeline draws three. Known TB lag, same class as `cooldownStartsAtStanceEnd` and `chargeModifiers`; ⛔ don't reconcile it by removing the cap.

nonHitting (non-hitting casts round, 2026-09-16 (docs/nonhitting-casts-round.md §1)): gcsim sucrose/burst.go:77-78: the wind-field ticks from f137 (after the 65f animation) are the Large Wind Spirit series.
abilities.description:
Sucrose hurls an unstable concoction that creates a Large Wind Spirit.
While it persists, the Large Wind Spirit will continuously pull in surrounding opponents and objects, launch nearby opponents, and deal Anemo DMG.

Elemental Absorption
If the Wind Spirit comes into contact with Hydro/Pyro/Cryo/Electro energy, it will deal additional elemental DMG of that type.
Elemental Absorption may only occur once per use.

passives.name: Catalyst Conversion
passives.caveat: Shown for the whole team, but in game only party members whose element matches the swirled one receive it — Anemo characters never do.
_curatorNotes: 2026-08-15: target was 'self', which was simply wrong — the buff never lands on Sucrose in game (gcsim asc.go a1() skips any char whose Base.Element != the swirled element, and she is Anemo). It also meant the effect was DROPPED before rendering: buffWindows' onReaction branch requires targetsTeamOrActive(), so the +50 EM drew nothing on the timeline at all. Now target:'teamExcludingSelf' with the element filter stated in the caveat — EffectTarget still has no element-filtered team type, so this over-renders (shows for every teammate) rather than under-rendering to nothing.

2026-08-15: added 'stellarSwirl' to the reaction OR-array — current Fandom talent text reads 'triggers a Swirl or Stellar Swirl reaction' (gcsim predates this; its a1() subscribes to the four base swirl events only). Inert for now: computeReactionsForCast does not emit stellarSwirl until its 7.0 mechanics are confirmed (see the note at notationParser.ts computeReactionsForCast). Authored anyway so the key is in place when emission lands.
2026-05-14 (Shape A reaction-key migration): trigger updated from broad `'swirl'` to an OR-array of the element-specific swirl keys.

↻ CAVEAT TRIMMED 2026-08-19 (ruthless pass): kept only the on-screen half. Full prior text: "Shown for the whole team, but in game only party members whose element matches the swirled one receive it — Anemo characters never do. Swirls of different elements run their own independent 8s windows."
passives.description: When Sucrose triggers a Swirl or Stellar Swirl reaction, all characters in the party with the matching element (excluding Sucrose) have their Elemental Mastery increased by 50 for 8s.

passives.name: Mollis Favonius
_curatorNotes: 2026-08-15: abilityType 'skill' → ['skill','burst']. gcsim a4() is called from BOTH skill.go and burst.go attack callbacks, and the talent text names both abilities. The old note claimed onHit.abilityType was single-valued — that has not been true since the array form landed (Escoffier C6), so only the E hit was firing and a Sucrose Q raised no EM at all.

2026-08-15: value 20 → { type:'scaling', stat:'em', ratio:20 }. The buff is 20% OF Sucrose's EM (gcsim: c.a4Buff[EM] = c.NonExtraStat(EM) * .20), not a flat +20 — the old flat value rendered as '+20 EM', off by roughly an order of magnitude on any real build. ratio is in PERCENTAGE POINTS per the BuffValue.scaling JSDoc, so 20 (not 0.2, as an earlier note guessed against the pre-correction renderer); it displays as '~20% EM'.

2026-08-15: snapshottable false → true. gcsim computes a4Buff once at trigger time from NonExtraStat(EM) and the receivers read that frozen slice for the whole 8s; Fandom's Gameplay Notes agree ('The Elemental Mastery buff snapshots on cast'), which is why an EM bump gained on the cast itself (Gilded Dreams 4pc, Etherlight Spindlelute) is captured and passed on.
Migrated to onHit ability:skill 2026-05-09 (F1).
passives.description: When Astable Anemohypostasis Creation - 6308 or Forbidden Creation - Isomer 75 / Type II hits an opponent, increases all party members' (excluding Sucrose) Elemental Mastery by an amount equal to 20% of Sucrose's Elemental Mastery for 8s.

constellations.name: Chaotic Entropy
constellations.caveat: Not modeled: the party-wide 20% DMG bonus for the absorbed element, or the further 8.6% Hexerei party members get.
_curatorNotes: [Hexerei] Permanent patch, NOT count-gated: gcsim internal/characters/sucrose/cons.go:47-59 c6() adds .20 elemental DmgP to every party member and +0.0857142 more when that member's own IsHexerei is set — no GetHexereiCount() check. Per-receiver faction routing is not expressible (EffectTarget has no faction subset and the existing effect is target:'team'), so the extra 8.57142 is stated in the caveat rather than modeled; the authored value:20 is unchanged.

Stub-with-caveat (decided 2026-05-14, onAbsorption category): manual trigger preserved because absorbed-element state is null-resolving in the planner. The duration is intentionally left absent. gcsim source: c6Absorb on every absorption tick, 6s base / 8s at C2+ (would need duration:6 + a durationModifier for C2 if ever upgraded to a deterministic trigger). ↻ CORRECTED 2026-09-15 (essential-characters T0): the '6s base / 8s at C2+' above is the BURST's duration (burst.go 360/480f), not C6's. gcsim c6() is called ONCE, when absorbCheck resolves an element (burst.go:112), and adds a modifier.NewBaseWithHitlag('sucrose-c6', 60*10) — 10s from the absorption. The kit text says 'during its duration', which reads as the burst's; the two sources disagree, so ⚠️ settle which before ever authoring a duration here.

↻ 2026-08-18: the note above used to end "the canonical burst-window-bound visualization is implicit; reviewer toggling the buff during a Sucrose Q window is the supported pattern". THERE IS NO TOGGLE AND THERE NEVER WAS. `trigger: 'manual'` has exactly one occurrence in src/ — the type declaration itself (src/lib/types/ability.ts:649). Nothing dispatches it, nothing renders it, there is no UI that turns it on. Corpus-wide that is 167 manual effects over 69 characters reaching no planner surface (rubric N1/D3). ⛔ Never rewrite a manual-trigger caveat into 'add it manually' — 'Not modeled' is the accurate phrasing, and this ability's caveat already says exactly that.

⚠️ The effect is NOT entirely invisible, and that is worth knowing before anyone deletes it as dead weight: `deriveCapabilities` filters by effect TYPE, not by trigger, so this buff still produces a Team Builder capability claim — verified 2026-08-18, `deriveCharacterCapabilities('sucrose')` emits {kind:'buff', detail:'allDmgBonus', target:'team', minConstellation:6, source: constellation Chaotic Entropy}. The TB says Sucrose is a team allDmgBonus buffer at C6; the planner draws nothing.

⏭ WORK ITEM if this is ever upgraded: the blocker named above ('absorbed-element state is null-resolving') is still real — there is no absorption in the sim at all (rubric N13; grep for `absorb` over src/lib finds no path, and gauge.ts's anemo case emits `swirl` with an `of` key without re-applying the swirled element). What HAS changed since 2026-05-14 is that the surrounding machinery would carry it: an `onCast` buff on this constellation entry would draw, and constellation gating at collection (effectCollection.ts `effectSourcesAtConstellation`) now keeps a C6 bar and its caveat out of a C0 rotation for free. The missing primitive is an absorbed-element resolution, not a trigger or a gate.

[A7] C6's +20% DMG bonus fires per burst cast when the burst absorbs one of Pyro/Hydro/Cryo/Electro; the timeline can't resolve which element absorbs, so it is authored as a team-wide manual-trigger window rather than a per-element buff.

[A7] In game the bonus routes only to the absorbed element (e.g. a Pyro DMG bonus), so the rendered team-wide value is an upper bound for teammates dealing off-element damage. ↻ 2026-08-18: 'the rendered team-wide value' is stale for the same reason as the toggle above — the manual trigger renders NOTHING on the timeline, so there is no over-broad bar for a reader to mistake. The routing claim itself stays true and is the reason the ability caveat lists the bonus as not modeled rather than describing a bar.

↻ 2026-09-21 (manual-trigger retirement, docs/manual-trigger-retirement-round.md). C6 "Chaotic Entropy" — effects[0] (buff allDmgBonus 20, team) DEFERRED. gcsim: `~/Code/gcsim/internal/characters/sucrose/burst.go:103-120` — `absorbCheck()` polls `Combat.AbsorbCheck(…Pyro, Hydro, Electro, Cryo)` from frame 136 every 18f until an element resolves into `c.qAbsorb`; on the first success it calls `c6()` ONCE. `cons.go:45-60` then adds `attributes.EleToDmgP(c.qAbsorb) = .20` to every party member for `60*10` frames, `+0.085714` more for members with `IsHexerei` — ⚠️ no `GetHexereiCount()` gate, so the Hexerei top-up is unconditional per receiver. Retain — `c6()` is called ONCE, at `burst.go:112`, the instant `absorbCheck` resolves an element (⛔ not per tick — the "6s base / 8s at C2" figures in the older note are the BURST's duration, `burst.go` 360/480f, not C6's); `EleToDmgP(c.qAbsorb)` routes the 20% to the absorbed element alone; the `+0.085714` Hexerei top-up is per-receiver and uncounted (`cons.go:53-56`); and the real blocker is that there is no absorption anywhere in `src/lib` — `gauge.ts`'s anemo case emits `swirl` with an `of` key without re-applying the swirled element. ⚠️ The authored `allDmgBonus` is a genuine over-claim in kind, not just in scope — it buffs every element for every teammate where the game buffs one, which is why deleting it now is an improvement even before the restore. ⚠️ The Hexerei top-up: `activeCharFaction` resolves only in the per-segment slice with `target: "active"` (the Linnea A4 shape), so a `target: "active"` + `{"type":"activeCharFaction","faction":"hexerei"}` twin at `value: 8.571429` would draw for an on-field Hexerei receiver — ⛔ but it would miss their off-field damage entirely, and the four element effects are `target: "team"`, so the pair cannot share a stat without the active-target pass's stat-dedupe silently keeping whichever was authored first. Keep it caveated. ⚠️ Deleting this effect also removes a live Team Builder claim: `deriveCharacterCapabilities('sucrose')` currently emits `{kind:'buff', detail:'allDmgBonus', target:'team', minConstellation:6}` — verified 2026-08-18 — so the TB stops calling C6 Sucrose a team all-damage buffer, which is correct and should be expected in the diff.
